rules.statement: report uses numbered sections with lettered items (1.a, 1.b, ...) so findings can be referenced and resolved one at a time
locations referenced by description or quoted snippet of surrounding text, never line numbers
proposed examples show good and bad versions side by side, each with a caption explaining why it is good or bad
a call-out quote is proposed for the start of every section, distilling its most important point or central thesis
the report states how each > EDITOR: directive was resolved

excluded.reason: fix spelling directly, everything else reported — compliance-cost rule, pressure-testing track
fact-check verification effort is compliance-cost; References-section element is downstream of web tools the read-only eval agent is denied
in-place spelling/grammar editing as the only directly applied category — compliance-cost, pressure-testing track
what to audit (structure/ambiguity) — no competing artifact shape
propose illustrations and analogies prescribes content, not form
repetition evaluation rubric; 'evaluate every occurrence' is compliance-cost, pressure-testing track
how to resolve EDITOR lines; reporting of resolutions covered by R-audit-report-04 entry
documented facts (80-char code-line limit, [label](url) link format) — retrieval-testing track
concreteness quality bar for proposals, not a competing document form
checklist restates body rules; no independent rule to violate
